records.query: Need the patient's viral PCR/serology panel results (e.g., HSV, VZV, enterovirus) and skin biopsy histopathology report, as these are core tests to confirm a viral mucocutaneous eruption and distinguish it from autoimmune bullous disease or sexually transmitted infection.

Need the actual results of the viral PCR/serology panel (HSV, VZV, enterovirus) and skin biopsy histopathology, including direct immunofluorescence if performed, as these are essential to confirm a viral mucocutaneous eruption and exclude autoimmune bullous disease or sexually transmitted infection.

Need the patient's viral serology and PCR panel (HSV, VZV, enterovirus, SARS-CoV-2) along with skin biopsy histopathology results, as these are essential to confirm a viral mucocutaneous eruption and distinguish it from autoimmune and drug-induced causes.

Need the direct immunofluorescence (DIF) result from perilesional skin and syphilis/HIV serology, as DIF is essential to exclude autoimmune bullous disease and serology helps rule out sexually transmitted infection, complementing the already requested viral PCR and histopathology to confirm a viral mucocutaneous eruption.

Need the patient’s SARS-CoV-2 and HSV/VZV/enterovirus PCR/serology results plus skin biopsy histopathology with direct immunofluorescence; these are essential to confirm viral mucocutaneous eruption and exclude autoimmune bullous disease or sexually transmitted infection.

Need the evidence text reporting the patient’s SARS-CoV-2 PCR/antibody results, HSV/VZV/enterovirus PCR/serology, and skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence findings; these pending results are decisive to confirm a viral mucocutaneous eruption and to differentiate infection-associated erythema multiforme from autoimmune bullous disease or sexually transmitted infection.

Need Mycoplasma pneumoniae serology and a detailed history of prior oral/genital herpes episodes, COVID-19 vaccination status, and all medications/vaccines in the past 8 weeks (including OTC and herbal), as these are essential to identify the specific viral trigger, distinguish COVID-19 from HSV- or Mycoplasma-associated erythema multiforme, and exclude drug-induced eruption.

bindings.label: 17-year-old male presents with 3 days of mouth pain and nonpainful penile erosions
One week prior, he experienced transient anosmia and ageusia that spontaneously resolved; he denied fever, cough, dyspnea, rhinorrhea, and gastrointestinal symptoms
He had taken acetaminophen and ibuprofen before presenting to the emergency department, but no medications before the onset of his mucocutaneous eruption

Physical examination showed he was afebrile with normal vital signs (respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 97%); findings included shallow erosions of the vermilion lips and hard palate, circumferential erythematous erosions of the periurethral glans penis, and 5 small vesicles on the trunk and upper extremities, with the remainder of the examination unremarkable
